Evelyn/Laura,

Thanks for the ping. Quick read: the W-9 looks handwritten-signed and the EIN in the header doesn't perfectly match the bank letter OCR. Two pragmatic paths here (ranked by speed):

1) Provisional PO with KYC hold (recommended): issue PO, set invoice routing to AP mailbox, hold payment until we receive one piece of stronger evidence (signed bank letter with company letterhead + copy of corporate filing).

2) Full verification before PO: ask vendor for IRS CP575/letter, or notarized bank letter, or a short video notarization showing signer and corporate documents (we accepted video-notarized bank letters once before).

I've attached a short procurement KYC checklist — please use the items marked "required for payment" when requesting follow-ups: procurement-kyc-checklist.pdf

If we go with option 1, procurement will create a provisional PO and add a milestone to clear the hold within 30 days. If option 2, we'll wait for docs and then issue PO immediately. Karthik: any compliance constraints re: video-notary vs in-person notary for US entities?

Ben Carter
Procurement Specialist
Redwood Inference
